register.name: PAKIS (packaging register, separate from PROTO)
register.notes: PAKIS fetched 2026-08-16 (Estonian, English option): board members get accounts from business-registry data, authenticate via ID-card/Mobile-ID/Smart-ID, and report packaging placed on market. Records feed both packaging and excise-tax reporting.

pro.ecoModulation: ETO sales-packaging fees: composite plastic (0.570) dearest, then mono plastic / plastic bottles (0.460); aluminium (0.290) above ferrous metal (0.260); wood cheapest (0.044). Group/transport packaging priced much lower.

extraTaxes.name: Pakendiaktsiis
extraTaxes.summary: Packaging excise duty (EMTA, confirmed 2026-08-16). Applies when packaged goods are first placed on the Estonian market. A packaging company that transfers its obligations by written contract to a licensed recovery organisation (ETO/TVO), or meets recovery targets itself, is EXEMPT — so joining a PRO is the economically sane route and avoids the excise.

notes: Rates from ETO's official 'teenustasud' (service fees) page (fetched 2026-08-16), müügipakend (sales packaging) service fee €/t → €/kg (before 24% VAT): glass 120 → 0.120, paper/cardboard mono 115 → 0.115, plastic mono & bottles 460 → 0.460 (composite plastic 570 → 0.570), ferrous metal 260 → 0.260 (shown as 'metal'; aluminium 290 → 0.290), beverage carton 115 → 0.115 ('composite'), wood 44 → 0.044. ETO's page also shows a lower 'actual cost' column per material. membershipRequired=false because the pakendiaktsiis excise is the legal alternative, but PRO membership both fulfils EPR and grants excise exemption. Excise rates are ~5–10× the PRO fee, so almost everyone joins a PRO.
